ERROR_ANALYSIS_TEXT: On BDG2 the Spearman correlation between per-building coverage and CV(RMSE) is -0.67 for CQR and -0.20 for PCS-CQR, i.e. PCS weakens the dependence of reliability on forecast difficulty. Across usage classes with at least 30 building × seed units, the coverage deviation falls in every class; the reduction is smallest for 'Lodging/residential'. Of 713 BDG2 target buildings (seed-averaged), 6 remain under-covered by PCS-CQR. Their median within-window level change |log(mean load weeks 5–8 / weeks 1–4)| is 0.289 versus 0.058 for the others (too few buildings for a test; descriptive only). On UCI, 1 of 270 clients remains under-covered (descriptive only).
ABSTRACT: Demand response, flexibility bidding and measurement-and-verification need day-ahead prediction intervals for individual buildings, often from the first days after metering starts. Interval methods are usually judged by coverage pooled over many buildings, which can hide buildings whose intervals are systematically too narrow. We evaluate per-building interval reliability during onboarding on 842 buildings at 10 sites (Building Data Genome 2) and 315 Portuguese electricity clients, under a building- and period-disjoint protocol with five seeds, every site held out in turn, cross-country transfer and stress tests. On one global quantile forecaster we compare pooled conformalised quantile regression (CQR) with self-only, adaptive (ACI), temporal-quantile-adjustment, hierarchical and quantile-shrinkage calibration and with a pseudo-count shrinkage of the score distribution towards each building's accumulating own scores (PCS). Pooled CQR left 18.2% (BDG2) and 9.1% (UCI) of new buildings more than five points below the 90 % target. PCS, with its pseudo-count chosen by leave-one-building-out for reliability, reduced these shares to 1.4% and 0.4% without a loss in interval score. A fixed one-week pseudo-count did equally well, as did quantile shrinkage tuned the same way, whereas ACI tuned purely for coverage was more reliable only with intervals 2.4 (BDG2) and 1.2 (UCI) times as wide. No strategy of comparable width repaired first-week under-coverage (PCS: 19.4% of BDG2 buildings). Similarity-weighted priors and onboarding-stage matching added nothing, leaving a one-parameter layer that costs well under a millisecond per building-day.
